q.t: What is the degree of 3x² + 5x − 7?
q.e: The degree is the highest power of the variable.

q.t: What is the coefficient of x² in 4x³ − 3x² + 1?
q.e: The number multiplying x², with its sign.

q.t: Which of these is a polynomial?
q.e: In a polynomial every power of the variable is a whole number (0, 1, 2 …). 1/x = x⁻¹ and √x = x^(1/2) break that rule.

q.t: If p(x) = x + 2, find p(1).
What is the zero of the polynomial x − 5?
q.e: A zero is the value of x that makes the polynomial 0: x − 5 = 0.

q.t: What is the degree of a non-zero constant polynomial such as 7?
What is the degree of a linear polynomial?
q.e: Linear means the highest power is 1, as in ax + b — its graph is a line.

q.t: How many terms does a binomial have?
If p(x) = 2x, find p(0).
A polynomial of degree 2 is called:
q.e: ‘Quad’ refers to squaring: the highest power is x².

q.t: If p(x) = x² − 3x + 2, find p(2).
q.e: 4 − 6 + 2 = 0, so 2 is a zero of p(x).

q.t: What is the zero of 2x + 3?
If p(x) = 5x − 4x² + 3, find p(−1).
What is the degree of (x² + 1)(x³ − 2)?
q.e: The highest term is x² × x³ = x⁵: degrees add when polynomials are multiplied.

q.t: Find the remainder when x² + 3x + 1 is divided by (x − 1).
q.e: Remainder theorem: the remainder on dividing by (x − a) is p(a). p(1) = 5.

q.t: Is (x − 2) a factor of x² − 4?
q.e: Factor theorem: (x − a) is a factor exactly when p(a) = 0. Here 4 − 4 = 0.

q.t: What are the zeros of x² − 9?
What is the degree of the zero polynomial?
q.e: The zero polynomial has no non-zero term, so there is no highest power to name.

q.t: What is the greatest number of zeros a cubic polynomial can have?
q.e: A polynomial of degree n has at most n zeros.

q.e: 2x − 1 = 0 at x = 1/2, so the remainder is p(1/2) = 1 + 1 − 1.

q.t: x³ + ax² + bx + 6 has (x − 2) as a factor and leaves remainder 3 when divided by (x − 3). Find a + b.
q.e: p(2) = 0 gives 2a + b = −7. p(3) = 3 gives 3a + b = −10. So a = −3 and b = −1.

q.t: Find the remainder when x⁵¹ + 51 is divided by (x + 1).
ax³ + 3x² − 13 and 2x³ − 5x + a leave the same remainder when divided by (x − 2). Find a.

p(x) = x⁴ − 2x³ + 3x² − ax + b leaves remainders 5 and 19 when divided by (x − 1) and (x + 1). Find the remainder when it is divided by (x − 2).
(x − 1) is a factor of k²x² − 2kx − 3. Find the positive value of k.
q.k: max(k for k in range(-9,10) if k*k-2*k-3==0)

q.t: Find the sum of all the coefficients in the expansion of (x² − x + 1)⁵.
q.e: The sum of the coefficients of any polynomial is its value at x = 1: (1 − 1 + 1)⁵.

q.t: 2 and −3 are the zeros of x² + (a + 1)x + b. Find b.
q.e: The polynomial is (x − 2)(x + 3) = x² + x − 6. Comparing, b = −6 (and a = 0).
